## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uppajjanti Sutta* is the tenth discourse of the sixth chapter (Jaccandhavagga) of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya (PTS Ud 72). The discourse addresses the theme that rival sectarians and philosophers shine only for as long as a Buddha has not arisen in the world. In his historical survey of Indian logic, Satis Chandra Vidhabhusana quotes the discourse's concluding inspired utterance (*udāna*) from Paul Steinthal's Pali Text Society edition: until the fully awakened Buddhas appear in the world, neither dialecticians (*takkikā*) nor their disciples achieve purification, nor do those bound to flawed views attain release from suffering [Vidhabhusana 1907].
